metadata.title: FOMC Summary of Economic Projections — federal funds rate dot plots
metadata.source: Federal Reserve, FOMC Summary of Economic Projections (SEP) projection materials, Figure 2 data tables (accessible HTML version), plus Table 1 memo line for the federal funds rate where available
metadata.source_name: Federal Reserve — FOMC Summary of Economic Projections
metadata.unit: Midpoint of target range or target level for the federal funds rate, percent
metadata.rounding: Dots are the Fed's published Figure 2 table values, rounded to the nearest 1/8 percentage point (1/4 point in 2012-2013, when the table used target levels), not the unrounded submissions. Published Table 1 medians are rounded to 0.1 percentage point; derived medians are exact on the 1/8-point grid.
metadata.anonymity: Dots are anonymous: no dot can be attributed to a person and no person's dots can be connected across vintages. This dataset shows the distribution moving over time, never an individual's path.
metadata.median_note: median_derived is computed from the dots for every (vintage, target_year). median_published is the Fed's Table 1 median and exists only for the 40 vintages from Sep 2016 onward (Table 1 is not in the accessible HTML before Sep 2016); for the 19 earlier vintages median_published is null and median_source is 'derived'. Never present a derived pre-Sep-2016 median as published.

longer_run.handling: Longer run has no calendar year and is NOT mapped to a fake year. Its dots and medians live in the separate `longer_run` section of this file; render them as a clearly labelled separate trace/plane or companion strip, never silently plotted at a calendar year such as 2030.

metadata.next_sep_note: Next SEP expected with the Dec 8-9, 2026 FOMC meeting. After it is published, re-run parse.py then assemble.py to add vintage 2026-12-09.
notes: Participant counts vary (14-19 per vintage-year); this is real, not missing data — seats vacant, and in 2026 only 18 participants submitted (Chair Warsh did not submit projections). In Jun/Sep 2026 one participant submitted no 2028/2029 dots.
The Longer run column is usually one dot short of the year columns (one participant does not submit a longer-run projection).
Empty = zero dots. Nothing is invented, interpolated, or imputed.
A dot is a participant's view of appropriate policy under their own outlook, not a forecast of what the Committee will do — do not plot a prediction-accuracy line from this dataset alone.
Outliers verified as real: Sep 2015 has the only sub-zero dots (one at -0.125% for end-2015 and one for end-2016); Jun 2023 and Sep 2023 each have one dot at 6.125%, the highest rate in the dataset.

longer_run.label: Longer run
longer_run.note: The longer-run federal funds rate (the neutral rate): participants' assessments of the appropriate rate in the longer run, with no calendar year attached. Shown here as a separate section — do not plot at a fake calendar year.
